name: Zoo Culture
who: Members-only gym and social club built by bodybuilder-YouTuber Bradley Martyn, a fixture for LA fitness creators and celebrities.
why: One of the first gyms built entirely from a creator's personal brand — turned Bradley Martyn's online fame into a real-world hangout-and-train destination.

name: Alphaland
who: 18.5-acre fitness compound built by YouTuber and Alphalete founder Christian Guzman — three gyms, courts, a sauna, a cafe, and a retail store under one roof.
why: The most ambitious creator-built gym in the world, a self-described 'Disney World for bodybuilders' that pulls visitors from across Texas and beyond.

name: Gymshark Lifting Club
who: Gymshark's own gym and innovation hub at its Solihull HQ, built to test product and shoot athlete content on-site.
why: The physical anchor of the biggest fitness-apparel creator economy in the world — sponsored athletes train and film here.

name: THENX Fitness Studio
who: Calisthenics training studio in Miami built around Chris Heria's THENX brand, the home base seen throughout his videos.
why: Anchors one of the largest calisthenics content ecosystems online; THENX and Heria Pro programs trace back to this floor.
reach: IG 2M (Chris Heria's personal following, verified 2026-08; the studio itself has no separate large account)

name: Iron Religion Gym
who: 24/7 hardcore bodybuilding and powerlifting gym on International Drive, open since 2016.
why: A regular stop for pros passing through Orlando for the Olympia Expo, built on old-school equipment mixed with modern plate-loaded gear.

name: Raw Athletic Club
who: Premium gym opened in 2024 by five-time Classic Physique Olympia champion Chris Bumstead's Raw Nutrition brand, with a barber, smoothie bar, and apparel shop attached.
why: The newest major creator-gym launch in bodybuilding, already drawing touring pros to train and film on camera.

name: Oxygen Gym
who: Leading hardcore bodybuilding gym brand in Kuwait, a hub for the country's outsized competitive bodybuilding scene.
why: The best-known gym name in Gulf bodybuilding culture, with a huge regional social following and heavy competition-prep traffic.

name: Strength Asylum
who: Strongman and bodybuilding gym in Hanley, Stoke-on-Trent, where former World's Strongest Man Eddie Hall trains full time.
why: Eddie Hall's huge YouTube following turns a local strongman gym into a UK pilgrimage stop for strength-sport fans.

name: 1st Phorm HQ
who: 185,000 sq ft supplement-company headquarters with a full athletic facility, turf field, and basketball court, built by 1st Phorm founder Andy Frisella's team.
why: One of the most-toured facilities on fitness YouTube — a supplement brand's HQ built as a destination gym, not just an office.
reach: IG 1M (1st Phorm brand account; approx 2026, not gym-specific)

name: Iron Addicts Gym
who: Powerbuilding gym in the LA area built around CT Fletcher, one of YouTube's earliest and loudest strength-training personalities.
why: CT Fletcher's viral intensity made Iron Addicts one of the first gyms to go famous purely through online video culture.

name: Overtime Athletics
who: Powerbuilding gym associated with boxer and content creator Mike Rashid, known for raw, no-frills strength content.
why: One of the earlier gyms to build an identity purely from documentary-style YouTube training footage.

name: Juggernaut Training Systems HQ
who: Powerlifting gym and coaching HQ built by Chad Wesley Smith's Juggernaut Training Systems, pairing sports-science content with a hardcore lifting floor.
why: A hub for competitive powerlifters and one of the most-followed programming brands in strength sport.
